embedded-page-metadata-01.graded_text: Tessel's own wrapper page emits the icon, title, and link preview tags in its initial server-rendered HTML, taken from the person's HTML when it is saved, rather than relying on the person's script or the inner document.

votes.e: D/project/docs/metadata.md:19 "Tessel owns the wrapper's metadata and renders it on the server. It takes the values from the page's own HTML when the page is published". Line 25: "When a page version is published, Tessel parses the static HTML once, without running it, and stores the result on the version record." Line 85: "the server renders `<title>{title} · Tessel</title>` and the page's icon links into the wrapper".

embedded-page-metadata-02.graded_text: Public and unlisted pages get page-specific previews, and unlisted pages keep noindex while still getting their real preview card.

votes.e: D/project/docs/metadata.md:59 "an unlisted page gets the same card as a public page. The only difference is indexing: <meta name=robots content=noindex> and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on the wrapper and on its preview image, and no sitemap entry."

embedded-page-metadata-03.graded_text: A private page answers any request not authorized for it, link-preview fetchers included, with a generic card that names only the product and carries no title, text, or image from the page.

votes.e: D/project/docs/metadata.md:63 "The server never returns its title, description, first paragraph, icon, image, or frame URL, not even to a signed-in member." Line 71: signed-out visitors, non-members, and missing addresses all get "the generic shell titled `Tessel`, the description `Sign in to view this page.`... and `noindex`". The description is generic product text, not page content, and line 119 says "Private pages have no preview image at all."

embedded-page-metadata-04.graded_text: Preview images are rendered in an environment that cannot write saved data or cause other side effects, and cannot reach private or internal networks or credentials, and a page load no person started, such as a link-preview fetcher running the page's script, cannot add saved data such as a poll vote.

votes.e: D does not say that image fetching or rendering can't reach private or internal networks or credentials. The closest lines are D/project/docs/metadata.md:102 "Remote URLs are fetched once, server-side, with a size cap (256 KB), a timeout, and a content-type allowlist" and line 116 "It's fetched once at publish (5 MB cap, raster types only), re-encoded". Neither blocks loopback, private, link-local, or metadata addresses. Line 117 renders the generated card "on request by an image route" and says nothing about that environment's credentials or network reach. The 251 write gate (lines 139-142) does pass its half, but the isolation half is missing.

embedded-page-metadata-05.graded_text: A page's own preview image is used when it declares one, and otherwise a preview is generated, so publishing never requires making an image.

votes.e: D/project/docs/metadata.md:114-117 "every public and unlisted page has one automatically: 1. The author's image, if the HTML declares `og:image` or `twitter:image`... 2. Otherwise, a generated Tessel card, 1200x630". Line 152: a failure "degrades to the fallbacks, and it never blocks publishing."

blocking: [opus-for-opus] Server-side fetches of URLs the author controls have no SSRF guard. D/project/docs/metadata.md:102 "Remote URLs are fetched once, server-side, with a size cap (256 KB), a timeout, and a content-type allowlist" and line 116 "fetched once at publish (5 MB cap, raster types only)" do not block loopback, private, link-local, or cloud-metadata addresses, and don't recheck redirects. An engineer building this as written would let any published page make Tessel's publish job request internal hosts, such as og:image=http://169.254.169.254/... or http://10.0.0.5/admin, and an internal image that decodes successfully would be re-hosted publicly as the preview card.
